slides.headline: 1) GPT-5 LAUNCHED AS ONE OF OPENAI'S LOW POINTS
slides.body: Three things broke at once: the routing system, the model quality, and the honesty of the numbers OpenAI used to sell it. One year later, all three have been replaced.

slides.headline: 2) ROUTING BROKE THE MOMENT GPT-5 LAUNCHED
slides.body: Automatic routing picked the lighter, cheaper option far too often. People paying for the full model kept getting cut-rate responses with no way to tell which version was handling their request.

slides.headline: 3) THE MODEL ITSELF FELL SHORT OF ITS OWN BENCHMARKS
slides.body: Even when routing worked, the outputs did not match the advertised scores. Tasks that older models had handled smoothly felt choppy or inconsistent. Early users called it a step sideways.

slides.headline: 4) CHARTCRIME WAS THE FINAL STRAW
slides.body: OpenAI put out comparison charts claiming GPT-5 led every rival. The AI community found cherry-picked tests and conditions. Chartcrime became the name for benchmark manipulation dressed up as proof.

slides.headline: 5) OPENAI RECOGNIZED THE PROBLEMS AND MADE A COMPLETE TURNAROUND
slides.body: Routing was rebuilt. The base model improved through a series of updates. The way OpenAI talked about benchmarks changed. Each problem named publicly got addressed publicly, and version 5.6 Sol now leads most head-to-head comparisons.

slides.headline: 6) VERSION 5.6 SOL ROSE TO THE TOP
slides.body: The current build, GPT-5.6 Sol, is what a year of iteration produced. Routing works, output quality matches the promise, and by most comparisons it is the best version of this model ever shipped.

slides.headline: SAVE THIS. MOST PEOPLE STILL PICTURE THE BROKEN LAUNCH VERSION.
slides.body: The ChatGPT running right now earned its spot. Save this for the next time someone says GPT-5 never got good.

caption:
Swipe to see what broke, what got rebuilt, and where GPT-5 stands today. 🔄

GPT-5's low-point launch one year ago, routing that defaulted to the wrong version on day one, a model that fell short of its own benchmarks, the chartcrime controversy that forced a public rethink, OpenAI's incremental turnaround through a series of updates, and version 5.6 Sol now sitting at the top.

A year of public failure produced the most-used AI tool at its current best. The version in most people's heads is still the broken launch build. The one running now is not. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we will show you what the current build can do for yours.
